<a name="MouseRegistry"></a>
## type [MouseRegistry](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/mouse.go#L66-L70>)

MouseRegistry manages hitboxes and mouse event handlers for zones across stack levels. It is the mirror of Registry \(keybindings\) for pointer/mouse events.

Usage \(via the fluent builder\):

```
app.Mouse().UpdateHitbox("sidebar", x, y, w, h)
app.Mouse().Zone("sidebar").OnClick(func(x, y int) { ... })
app.Mouse().Zone("panel").OnDrop(func(from string, x, y int) { ... })
```

Then, on each mouse event from the UI adapter:

```
router.HandleMouseEvent(msg.X, msg.Y, router.MouseEventClick)
```

```go [mouse.go]
}
```

<a name="MouseRegistry.ResolveZone"></a>
### func \(\*MouseRegistry\) [ResolveZone](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/mouse.go#L166>)

```go [mouse.go]
func (r *MouseRegistry) ResolveZone(stackLevel, px, py int) (string, bool)
```

ResolveZone performs hit\-testing: it finds the zone at \(px, py\) within the given stack level. Returns the zone ID and true on a hit, or \("", false\) when no zone contains the point.

When multiple hitboxes overlap, the first registered zone that matches wins.


UnregisterLevel removes all hitboxes and handlers for a specific stack level. Called automatically by the Router when a layer is popped to prevent memory leaks.

## type [Router](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/router.go#L14-L23>)

Router handles logical routing of keys and mouse events to the appropriate layer and zone.

```go [router.go]
type Router struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields

```

<a name="NewRouter"></a>
### func [NewRouter](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/router.go#L32>)

```go [router.go]
func NewRouter(cancel context.CancelFunc, getLogger func() contracts.Logger) *Router
```

NewRouter creates a new logical Key Router.

Auto\-focus is enabled by default: whenever a layer is pushed or popped via the low\-level [Stack.Push](<#Stack.Push>) / [Stack.Pop](<#Stack.Pop>) methods, the router automatically shifts keyboard focus to the new top layer's zone \(using the layer ID as the zone name\). Call [Router.SetAutoFocus](<#Router.SetAutoFocus>)\(false\) to disable this behaviour and manage focus manually via [Router.Focus](<#Router.Focus>).


Focus sets the currently focused zone for a given stack level. When auto\-focus is enabled this is called automatically on every push/pop; call it manually only when you need a non\-default zone name.

<a name="Router.PopLayer"></a>
### func \(\*Router\) [PopLayer](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/router.go#L151>)

```go [router.go]
func (r *Router) PopLayer()
```

PopLayer pops the topmost layer from the stack and — when auto\-focus is enabled — reverts keyboard focus to the new top layer. This is the high\-level alternative to calling Stack\(\).Pop\(\) and Focus\(\) separately.

```
router.PopLayer()
// equivalent to:
//   router.Stack().Pop()
//   router.Focus(newLevel, newTop)
```

<a name="Router.PushLayer"></a>
### func \(\*Router\) [PushLayer](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/router.go#L138>)

```go [router.go]
func (r *Router) PushLayer(layerID string)
```

PushLayer pushes layerID onto the stack and — when auto\-focus is enabled — immediately shifts keyboard focus to the new layer's zone \(zone name == layerID\). This is the high\-level alternative to calling Stack\(\).Push\(\) and Focus\(\) separately.

```
router.PushLayer("search")
// equivalent to:
//   router.Stack().Push("search")
//   router.Focus(newLevel, "search")
```


SetAutoFocus enables or disables automatic focus synchronisation with the stack. When enabled \(the default\), pushing or popping a layer automatically shifts keyboard focus to the new top layer's zone \(zone name == layer ID\).

Disable this if you manage focus manually via [Router.Focus](<#Router.Focus>).

<a name="Stack"></a>
## type [Stack](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/stack.go#L36-L45>)

Stack manages an array/slice of active UI layers.

Push and Pop return \*Stack to allow fluent chaining:

```
ctx.Stack().Push("search").Push("results")
ctx.Stack().Pop().Pop()
```

When a guard blocks an operation, the registered [Stack.OnPushBlocked](<#Stack.OnPushBlocked>) or [Stack.OnPopBlocked](<#Stack.OnPopBlocked>) callback is invoked instead of propagating an error. This keeps the happy path clean while giving you a single place to handle guard failures \(e.g., logging, showing a UI toast, or emitting an event\).

Register guard callbacks before performing push/pop operations:

```
ctx.Stack().
    OnPushBlocked(func(layer, reason string) {
        ctx.Logger().Warn("push blocked", "layer", layer, "reason", reason)
    }).
    OnPopBlocked(func(layer, reason string) {
        ctx.Logger().Warn("pop blocked", "layer", layer, "reason", reason)
    })
```

```go [stack.go]
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="Stack.AfterPop"></a>
### func \(\*Stack\) [AfterPop](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/stack.go#L74>)

```go [stack.go]
func (s *Stack) AfterPop(fn func(layerID string)) *Stack
```

AfterPop registers an observer that is called after every successful Pop. The observer receives the ID of the layer that was just removed \(i.e. the former top\). This is used internally by the Router to implement auto\-focus.

Calling AfterPop multiple times replaces the previous observer. Returns \*Stack for chaining.

<a name="Stack.AfterPush"></a>
### func \(\*Stack\) [AfterPush](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/stack.go#L61>)

```go [stack.go]
func (s *Stack) AfterPush(fn func(layerID string)) *Stack
```

AfterPush registers an observer that is called after every successful Push. The observer receives the ID of the layer that was just added. This is used internally by the Router to implement auto\-focus; most application code should use [Router.PushLayer](<#Router.PushLayer>) instead.

Calling AfterPush multiple times replaces the previous observer. Returns \*Stack for chaining.

<a name="Stack.BeforePop"></a>
### func \(\*Stack\) [BeforePop](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/stack.go#L142>)

```go [stack.go]
func (s *Stack) BeforePop(guard StackGuardFunc)
```

BeforePop registers a guard function that is called before every Pop. The layer argument is the layer that would be removed \(the current Top\). If any guard returns false, the Pop is cancelled.

Example:

```
stack.BeforePop(func(layer string) (bool, string) {
    if layer == "editor" && editor.HasUnsavedChanges() {
        return false, "unsaved changes — confirm before closing"
    }
    return true, ""
})
```

<a name="Stack.BeforePush"></a>
### func \(\*Stack\) [BeforePush](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/stack.go#L124>)

```go [stack.go]
func (s *Stack) BeforePush(guard StackGuardFunc)
```

BeforePush registers a guard function that is called before every Push. If any guard returns false, the Push is cancelled and the layer is not added. Guards are evaluated in registration order; the first rejection wins. The returned reason string is informational \(e.g. for logging or UI feedback\).

Example:

```
stack.BeforePush(func(layer string) (bool, string) {
    if layer == "settings" && !user.IsAdmin() {
        return false, "admin access required"
    }
    return true, ""
})
```


Layers returns a snapshot copy of the current layer slice, bottom to top.

<a name="Stack.OnPopBlocked"></a>
### func \(\*Stack\) [OnPopBlocked](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/stack.go#L104>)

```go [stack.go]
func (s *Stack) OnPopBlocked(fn func(layer, reason string)) *Stack
```

OnPopBlocked registers a callback that is invoked whenever a Pop is blocked by a registered guard. The callback receives the top layer name and the reason.

Calling OnPopBlocked multiple times replaces the previous callback. Returns \*Stack for chaining.

```go [stack.go]
func (s *Stack) OnPushBlocked(fn func(layer, reason string)) *Stack
```

OnPushBlocked registers a callback that is invoked whenever a Push is blocked by a registered guard. The callback receives the layer name that was rejected and the reason string returned by the guard.

Calling OnPushBlocked multiple times replaces the previous callback. Returns \*Stack for chaining:

```
ctx.Stack().
    OnPushBlocked(func(layer, reason string) {
        ctx.Emit("stack:push_blocked", map[string]any{"layer": layer, "reason": reason})
    })
```

<a name="Stack.Pop"></a>
### func \(\*Stack\) [Pop](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/stack.go#L190>)

```go [stack.go]
func (s *Stack) Pop() *Stack
```

Pop removes the top layer from the stack. Returns \*Stack for fluent chaining:

```
ctx.Stack().Pop().Pop()
```

If any registered guard blocks the pop, the layer is NOT removed and the [Stack.OnPopBlocked](<#Stack.OnPopBlocked>) callback \(if registered\) is invoked. Pop on an empty stack is a no\-op \(returns the Stack unchanged, no callback fired\).

<a name="Stack.Push"></a>
### func \(\*Stack\) [Push](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/stack.go#L156>)

```go [stack.go]
func (s *Stack) Push(layerID string) *Stack
```

Push adds a new layer to the top of the stack. Returns \*Stack for fluent chaining:

```
ctx.Stack().Push("base").Push("overlay")
```

If any registered guard blocks the push, the layer is NOT added and the [Stack.OnPushBlocked](<#Stack.OnPushBlocked>) callback \(if registered\) is invoked with the layer name and reason. The chain continues regardless — Push never panics.

<a name="StackGuardFunc"></a>
## type [StackGuardFunc](<https://github.com/gettako/tako/blob/main/internal/router/stack.go#L13>)

StackGuardFunc is a function that decides whether a stack transition is allowed. It receives the layer name that is about to be pushed or popped. Returning false blocks the operation. Returning an error also blocks and surfaces the reason.

```go [stack.go]
type StackGuardFunc func(layer string) (allow bool, reason string)
```
